subject: Hosted latency acceptance: p95/p99 envelope & streaming ops questions
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Lee <martin.lee@veridian.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted latency acceptance: p95/p99 envelope & streaming ops questions

Hey Martin — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can unblock the perf qualification run: 

Summary from our side:
- Goal: validate p95 <= 220 ms and p99 <= 420 ms end-to-end for your API surface (single-turn chatbot + streaming audio transcription fallback) against a production-like traffic envelope.
- Primary constraints you mentioned: 90% of requests are < 150 tokens; 10% include streaming with chunked responses; peak concurrency ~420 QPS during batch arrivals.

Asks / action items: 
1) You to share a 1-hour representative traffic trace + a small set of problematic traces (we can use sampling) — filename stub attached (veridian_p95_p99_profile.csv).
2) We will run two lanes on hosted:
   a) Baseline hosted config (nvlink-enabled, 16-bit quant) to measure p95/p99 at your envelope.
   b) Fallback flow that forces streaming chunking + KV prefetch to measure tail behavior.
3) Jonas (cc'd) will define exact probe harness and artifact names and will need a short shared SSH key or signed presigned URL to fetch traces during the run.
4) Clarify SLO acceptance criteria: is p99 <= 420 ms a hard requirement for cutover or an initial target for follow-up tuning?

Tentative schedule:
- Wed 11/08: data/trace delivery (your side)
- Thu 11/09: hosted probe window (we run controlled traffic, 2-3 hours)
- Fri 11/10: results & remediation plan

Attachments: veridian_p95_p99_profile.csv (sampled traffic), streaming-sample-trace.json (example streaming chunk timestamps).

If that matches, we'll queue a hosted probe and loop in infra for the runbook.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Martin Lee <martin.lee@veridian.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@veridian.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 10:01:34 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted latency acceptance: p95/p99 envelope & streaming ops questions

Evelyn — thanks for the crisp recap. Confirming a few things from our side: 

- We'll upload the 1-hour trace by COB Tuesday (11/07). It contains tokenized lengths and timestamps; we will also flag ~25 traces that produced user-visible lag in prod.
- p99 <= 420 ms is the gating requirement for our customer-facing streaming transcripts. p95 <= 220 ms is preferred but negotiable if p99 is solid.
- Peak concurrency: correction — 420 QPS is at traffic peaks but sustained peaks (15 min windows) are around 320 QPS. Bursts to 600 QPS happen during scheduled notifications but they tolerate higher latency.

One operational note: our auth tooling prohibits shared SSH keys; presigned S3 URLs (30 min) are preferred. I'll drop links once the upload completes.

Martin
Martin Lee
Staff SRE, Veridian Health
martin.lee@veridian.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Martin Lee <martin.lee@veridian.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 13:07:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency acceptance: p95/p99 envelope & streaming ops questions

Martin / Evelyn — small technical clarifications so the probe harness maps to Veridian's production: 

1) Traffic shaping: we will replay your 1-hour trace as-is and also run a 30-minute scaled window at 1.5x sustained to emulate your burst tolerance. Please confirm if multiplying client-side arrival timestamps is acceptable (we'll keep token sequences intact).

2) Streaming workload: how do you chunk server-side streaming? Two common patterns: 
   - chunk-by-token-window (approx 32 token windows), or
   - time-based chunks (every 80ms).
Please indicate which you use for realtime transcripts — the chunking pattern materially impacts p99.

3) Auth and artifacts: presigned S3 URLs are fine. Martin, if you can include HMAC header expectations in a short README it will speed the run.

4) Probe metrics: we'll publish per-probe p50/p95/p99, API-level tail histograms, and a capture of KV cache hit-rates for the streaming paths. If p99 spikes > 500ms for more than 2 consecutive windows we'll automatically run a quantized fallback and record comparison artifacts.

Low-priority ask: do you have any client-side connection pooling (keepalive) behavior that would affect concurrency? We assume short-lived connections for the probe unless you tell us otherwise.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Lee <martin.lee@veridian.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted latency acceptance: p95/p99 envelope & streaming ops questions

Perfect — thanks Martin/Jonas. Next steps captured: 
- Martin: upload traces to presigned S3 by 2028-11-07 COB + include README with HMAC notes.
- Jonas: prepare probe config (replay + 1.5x scaled window) and list of exact artifacts we'll publish after the run.
- Camila: I'll coordinate calendar & infra access; blocking calendar invite to follow for Thu 11/09 09:00-13:00 PT (probe window).

I'll mark the deal record and note the gating requirement (p99 <= 420 ms). If we see p99 regressions we'll capture remediation steps and propose configuration-level mitigations (batching, KV prewarm, or quantized path) in the results doc.

Thanks all — looking forward to the run.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
